chapter_title: The Explanation of the Peace, what it is; the Right Hand; the Kiss; the Salutation.
chapter_note: This chapter presents the five ritual signs (peace, right hand, kiss, salutation, laying on of hands) as cosmic archetypes established by the First Man's descent to battle and ascent from victory. The oldest teaching layer is a two-series cosmological narrative: Series 1 (descent, ¶3–9) is nearly pure substrate; Series 2 (ascent, ¶10–14) preserves substrate cosmic narrative overlaid with editorial bridge formulas ('appropriate to the mystery of X, this Y has come about among mankind'). Significant editorial fatigue confirmed: substrate drops from 6.68→2.02 while institutional rises 2.18→9.16 in the second half. The chapter transitions from pure cosmic teaching through mixed cosmic+bridge to fully institutional application (¶16–19) and exhortation (¶21–24). A Light Form/Daēnā passage (¶20) preserves genuinely ancient Persian imagery of the soul's cosmic encounter. The Psalm 110:1 citation in ¶14 is a clear editorial insertion within cosmic narrative. The five-fold enumeration structure (peace, right hand, kiss, salutation, laying on of hands) is the substrate's organizational spine.

paragraphs.core_text: This peace and this greeting that occur in the world, [from w]hom [did they come fo]rth? Or likewise, the right hand that occurs in [the world, it being h]onoured by mankind, of whom is it? Or the mystery of the kiss that they embrace one another with, [ ... ]? Or who is the one that reveals this salutation with which they make obeisance to one another? Or this laying on of hands, which an immensely great one bequeaths upon his inferior, giving him an honour and making him great; of whom is this laying on of hands?
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped dialogue frame formula: 'Once again the disciples questioned the apostle, saying [to him]:' — standard Kephalaia opening attribution with no cosmological content.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The substantive questions define the five-fold teaching structure. They reference worldly practices ('occur in the world') but as the teaching PROBLEM, not as editorial application. The questions belong to the Persian pedagogical tradition — they establish what the teaching will map. High dialogue_frame (12.96) and institutional (9.26) scores reflect frame formula and 'laying on of hands' vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: these five signs are the mystery of the First Man. He came forth with them from the aeon of light. Also, when he finished his contest, he went up with these good signs. They received him into the aeons of light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped dialogue frame and editorial introduction: 'Then he says to his disciples: You have questioned me about these five lessons. Now, they are displayed in the world as miniatures, being made little; and yet indeed they are great and honoured. I am the one who can reveal to you their mystery! So,' — contains frame attribution, first-person authority claim ('I am the one who can reveal'), and editorial framing of the correspondence principle.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The core teaching identifies the five signs with the First Man and establishes the two-part structure (departure and return). 'They are displayed in the world as miniatures' is an interesting cosmological principle about correspondence but is embedded in the editorial introduction and first-person claims. The core cosmological content maps the five signs to the First Man's journey — both sides within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.38⟩ The first peace is the one that the gods and the angels in the land of light gave to the First Man; when he comes out against the enemy. The gods and the angels were walking with him; escorting him, giving to him their peace and power, and their blessing and fortification. This is the first peace that the gods and the angels gave to the First Man; as he comes forth from the aeon of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Systematic cosmological teaching: maps the first peace to a cosmic event (gods and angels blessing the First Man at departure). Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system: cosmic beings → cosmic action. The enumeration marker 'The first peace' opens the five-fold descent series. No editorial application, no bridge to the world.

paragraphs.core_text: The first right hand is the one that the Mother of Life gave to the First Man; when he comes out to the contest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Second element of the five-fold descent enumeration. Extremely concise — maps 'first right hand' to Mother of Life → First Man. High substrate density (20.83) confirms. The brevity itself may be a mark of antiquity — the teaching IS the mapping, with no elaboration.

paragraphs.core_text: The first kiss is this one with which the Mother of Life embraced the First Man; as he separates from her, coming down to the contest. Even all the gods and the angels who are in the aeons of light were making to embrace him! [ ... ] all of them also, and the church tutelaries (?), and the kinsfolk who belong to the household of his people. They were making to embrace him as [he] separates from them, accompanying him out, embracing him with the kiss of affection and love.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate: third element of the descent enumeration. The 'church tutelaries (?)' — the translator's question mark indicates uncertainty about the Coptic term. In context these are cosmic beings in the aeons of light, likely a cosmic category rendered with institutional vocabulary by the Coptic translators. 'Kinsfolk who belong to the household of his people' is cosmic household language. The institutional score (2.2) is triggered by this uncertain term; the content is entirely cosmic narrative.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.39⟩ The first salutation is the salutation with which the First Man made obeisance; when he comes out [to the depths] below. He was bending his knees, making obeisance to the God of truth, and all the aeons [of light] who belong to the household of his people; entreating them for a power to escort him, as he comes forth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Fourth element of the descent enumeration. Maps the first salutation to the First Man's obeisance before departure. 'The God of truth' and 'the household of his people' are cosmic references. Both sides of the mapping remain within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The first laying on of hands is the one that the Mother of Life bequeathed upon the head of the First Man. She armed him and made him mighty. She laid hands on him, and sent him to the battle. He descended. He completed his struggle with the great powers and the enmity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate. Fifth and final element of the descent enumeration. The institutional score (9.43) is triggered by 'laying on of hands' but here this is the COSMIC ARCHETYPE — the Mother of Life performing the act on the First Man. This is precisely the kind of passage where institutional vocabulary appears in substrate because the substrate IS the origin-narrative of the institutional practice. 'He descended. He completed his struggle' has the terse, process-oriented quality of the oldest layer.

paragraphs.core_text: By the [se] five signs and these five myst[e]ri[es] the First Man came forth from the aeons of light against the enemy. He humbled him. He was victorious against him by them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate summary closing the descent series. High substrate density (15.62). Terse, impersonal, process-oriented: 'He humbled him. He was victorious against him by them.' This is the summarizing voice of the oldest teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, when he ascended from the war, he came in to the kingdom of the household of his people by these five mysteries!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate. Transitional summary bridging descent to ascent series — the First Man returns with the same five signs. The substrate score is 0.0 (the vocabulary counter missed it) but the content is unambiguously cosmic narrative: First Man ascending to the kingdom of his people. No editorial application, no contemporary reference.

paragraphs.core_text: The peace with which [he ascen]ded is the peace that the summons gave to him, [w]hen it was sent forth from the [Fa]ther of Life. It gave him the peace in the world of darkness. Also, that peace with which he descended is th[e sam]e as the one with which he ascended from the struggle!
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped editorial bridge: 'Therefore, appropriate to the my[s]tery of that peace, which the summons gave the First Man, did this peace here and now come about. It was named and heard among the powers of the Father.' — the 'appropriate to the mystery' formula connects the cosmic archetype to worldly practice ('here and now'). One side of the mapping reaches outside the cosmic system to contemporary human experience.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The ascent series begins. The cosmic content introduces 'the summons' — a specific cosmic entity from the emanation hierarchy — giving peace to the First Man in darkness. This cosmological detail (different agent from the descent series) suggests genuine substrate. The bridge formula 'appropriate to the mystery... here and now' is the editor's consistent method of connecting each ascent element to worldly practice.

paragraphs.core_text: this second right hand is the one that the Living Spirit gave the First Man, when he [brou]ght him upward out from the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped connective 'Again,' and editorial bridge: 'Appropriate to [the] mystery [of t]hat right hand this right hand has come about; the one that occurs in the [midst of] mankind, as they give it to their companions, [it b]eing honoured and [ ... ]' — same 'appropriate to the mystery' bridge formula connecting cosmic archetype to 'mankind' and worldly practice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The cosmic content is precise: the Living Spirit (not the Mother of Life from the descent series) gives the right hand. Different cosmic agents for descent vs. ascent is a mark of genuine cosmological knowledge. The bridge formula follows the same pattern as ¶10.

paragraphs.core_text: this second kiss is the one with which the [Father o]f Life and the Mother of the living embraced the First Man, when he ascended from the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped connective 'Also,' and editorial bridge: 'Again, this kiss occurs among mankind, as they make to embrace their companions with it; whether then [they] go away from home and be far from their friends, or else [if] they approach one another, according to the mystery of (the First Man).' — the bridge maps the cosmic kiss to worldly social practice, elaborating on when humans embrace. This elaboration of worldly customs is editorial extension.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The cosmic content again involves precise agents: 'the Father of Life and the Mother of the living' — both receiving the First Man. This specificity (both divine parents embrace him on return) is characteristic of the substrate's systematic cosmic knowledge. The editorial bridge is more expansive here, adding worldly social detail.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.40⟩ [The] second salutation with which the First Man made obeisance [ ... this] time to the God of truth and [ ... ] the blessed aeons and al[l] the aeons [ ... the] whole [land] of light, whe[n] the Father of Life and the Mother of the living brought the Man upward from the abyss of the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped editorial bridge: 'Appropriate to the mystery of the second salutation this salutation has come about; this one that occurs today in the midst of mankind, as they make obeisance to one another, doing an honour to their companions.' — same bridge formula as ¶10–11, with 'today' explicitly anchoring to editorial present.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extensive lacunae in the cosmic portion, but the surviving text describes the First Man's obeisance to the God of truth and all the aeons of light upon being brought upward. 'The abyss of the struggle' is cosmic geography. The bridge formula contains 'today' — the most explicit temporal marker of editorial present in this series.

paragraphs.core_text: The second laying on of hands is this: When the Living Spirit brought the First Man upward from the war, he saved him from all the surging waves. He brought him upward, he gave him ease in the great aeons of light, which belong to the household of his people. He set [him] firmly before the Father, the Lord of the totality. He received this great laying on of hands that he may become leader of his brethren in the new aeon.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped (1) Psalm 110:1 citation: 'Now, when he went up before the great Father of the lights, a voice came forth to him from the heights, saying: Make my son, my first-born, to sit at my right hand side, until I set all his enemies for a footstool under his feet.' — the oldest teaching expounds, it does not cite; this is a scriptural citation applied to the cosmic narrative. Stripped (2) editorial bridge: 'Again, appropriate to the mystery of the second laying on of hands, this laying on of hands has come about; the one that occurs in the midst of mankind as they lay hands on one another, the great giving authority to the lesser.' — same bridge formula as ¶10–13.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The most complex mixed paragraph. The cosmic narrative is detailed: Living Spirit saving the First Man from 'surging waves,' setting him before 'the Father, the Lord of the totality,' and the new aeon. The Psalm 110 citation ('sit at my right hand... footstool under his feet') is the clearest marker of editorial insertion — a scriptural text applied to the cosmic narrative. This enters via the NT/OT, not from the substrate tradition. The 'new aeon' terminology IS substrate; 'leader of his brethren in the new aeon' describes the First Man's cosmic role.

paragraphs.core_text: These five mysteries and these five signs came about first in the divine. these mysteries were not at the beginning amongst the powers of Darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped editorial transition: 'They were proclaimed in this world by an apostle. Mankind has been taught them; and they have instituted them in their midst [ ... but]' — references apostolic proclamation and human institution of the mysteries, connecting cosmic teaching to the editorial present.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Transitional paragraph. The two retained statements are genuine cosmological assertions: (1) the five signs originated in the divine realm, (2) they did not exist among the powers of Darkness. Both sides stay within the cosmic system. The removed material bridges to 'an apostle' and 'mankind' — the editorial present. This paragraph marks the seam between the substrate teaching (¶3–14) and the institutional application (¶16–19).

Fully institutional. 'The Light Mind... shall choose his church' applies the cosmic entity to church formation. 'With these five lessons he shall choose his church' is institutional — one side of the mapping reaches into the organized Manichaean community. High institutional score (20.83) confirms. This begins the church-application section that runs through ¶19.

Fully institutional. Describes a step-by-step process of church admission using the five signs: receive peace → become child of peace → elected to the faith → receive right hand → drawn to church. This is catechetical procedure, not cosmic mapping. 'He is elected to the faith' and 'cause him to approach the church' are institutional process language.

Fully institutional. 'Becomes a child of the church,' 'he makes obeisance to the holy church,' 'the hope of the faith, good works' — all institutional community language. Continues the catechetical sequence from ¶17. High institutional score (21.15).

Institutional. Describes completion of the five-sign reception process: 'conformed and built up in the truth,' 'become fulfilled people,' 'make obeisance and give glory to the God of truth.' The five signs are applied to community formation, not cosmic process. 'They shall come in to the Light Mind with these good signs' maps the institutional process to a cosmic entity but the primary domain is institutional.

paragraphs.core_text: At the time of their coming forth, the Light Form shall come forth before them; and she redeems them from the darkness to the light [ ... ] This Light Form calms the person, with the kiss and her quiet, from fear of the demons w[ho de]stroy his body. By her asp[ec]t and her image [the] heart of the elect one, who is come forth from his bo[d]y, shall be calm for [him]. Afterwards, the angel who h[o]lds the victory prize extends to him the right hand. And it draws him out of the abyss of his body, and accepts him in with the [k]iss and love. That soul shall make obeisance to its red[eem]er, who is this Light Form.
paragraphs.removed_material: Stripped frame marker 'Once again:' and institutional/eschatological closure: 'And also, at the inst[ant when ... ] he shall be perfected and increased according to [ ... / ... ] in the household of the living ones, with the go[ds] and the angel[s] and all the apostles and the chosen. [An]d he receives the crown [ ... ] glory in the life for ever.' — 'all the apostles and the chosen' is institutional vocabulary; 'crown... glory in the life for ever' is devotional closure language.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The Light Form (Daēnā) encounter is genuinely ancient Persian cosmological imagery — the heavenly counterpart meeting the departing soul. Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system: Light Form (cosmic being) → soul (cosmic light particle). The angel with the victory prize, the right hand, the kiss, the obeisance — all map the five signs to a cosmic process (soul's ascent). The ending shifts to institutional language ('apostles and chosen') and devotional closure ('crown... glory... for ever'). The substrate score of 0.0 reflects the vocabulary counter's limitations — the cosmic content uses soul/Light Form vocabulary rather than the typical substrate markers.

Classic exhortation/devotional closure. 'Concerning this I tell you, my brethren and my limbs' — standard first-person address formula. 'Let you find these five signs in your hands' — injunction to practice. 'I have brought this to you from the household of the living, out from the Father who sent me' — apostolic authority claim. High exhortation score (20.97) confirms.

Institutional. Audience-directed recapitulation: 'you have understood about the first peace and the first right hand...' — directs the community's comprehension. 'These five signs that I have brought' — first-person apostolic claim. 'You may part from the world' — eschatological promise tied to community membership. The paragraph uses the substrate's enumeration ('first peace... first right hand... first kiss') as content but the voice is institutional — directing the community.

Flagged as PROBABLE EDITORIAL EXTENSION by the seam detector. Fully institutional: 'the teachers and the deacons and the presbyters' — church offices; 'I have laid hands on' — first-person institutional authority; 'whoever will reject and disdain it... commits sin subject to God' — enforcement of institutional hierarchy. The highest institutional score in the chapter (33.66). This extends the laying on of hands teaching to enforce clerical authority — a classic editorial seam where cosmic teaching is appropriated for institutional legitimation.

Exhortation/devotional closure. Heavily damaged text. 'You, my beloved ones' — classic address formula. 'Your heart,' 'listen to him,' 'every deed that you do' — moral injunction fragments. 'He turns to you... from you the afflictions' — eschatological promise. This is the standard Kephalaia closure pattern: moral application appended to the completed teaching sequence.
